incidents.name: HenloKart ETH transfer helper credits contract balance
incidents.notes: HenloKart's ETH transfer helper treated from == msg.sender as authority to pay out of the contract's own balance rather than requiring msg.value, so a zero-value race commitment was funded from the contract, and an inverted cancel-lock check let the attacker cancel immediately and take the fake deposit back.

sources.ref: onchain review: proxy 0x27fafc210e4b240786d9ef3aa44399fb7e107f6f created 2025-02-22T18:32:29Z by 0x72c3c8b0cacdf6e36b39c9462a42756b2a294ccb, not the attack-tx sender 0xc2b2197ca4b2ee3b4eb61fc59e6d592d04a2e26a; a single EIP-1967 Upgraded event at deployment installs 0x5e30de98d133f956e118233ed8e054e0f5e65781, so the executing code was 3.57 days old. 0.59 ETH x $2,467.27 at the incident timestamp (DefiLlama) = $1,456.
